title: Quasi-coherent algebras on qcqs spaces are directed colimits of finitely presented algebras
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Assume $X$ is quasi-compact, meaning that it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme, and quasi-separated, meaning that its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact on affine scheme tests. A morphism is quasi-compact on affine scheme tests when its pullback over each affine scheme has quasi-compact source. Let $\mathcal A$ be a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras on the small etale site whose underlying module is quasi-coherent [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. There exist a small nonempty directed set $I$, quasi-coherent commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras $\mathcal A_i$, algebra maps $\alpha_{ji}:\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal A_j$ for $i\le j$ satisfying the identity and composition laws, and compatible algebra maps $\alpha_i:\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal A$, such that each $\mathcal A_i$ is finitely presented as an algebra: for every affine etale chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$, the $R$-algebra $\mathcal A_i(U)$ has a presentation $R[T_1,\ldots,T_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ for finite $n,m$. The cocone $(\mathcal A,(\alpha_i))$ is colimiting in quasi-coherent commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]: for every such algebra $\mathcal C$, compatible algebra maps $\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal C$ factor uniquely through an algebra map $\mathcal A\to\mathcal C$. Neither the transition maps nor the maps to $\mathcal A$ are required to be injective.

proof.text: The atlas form of quasi-compactness in the statement implies that $|X|$ is quasi-compact by the last assertion of [lem-a1-space-finite-affine-subatlas]. Thus [lem-sfb-space-module-fp-directed-approximation] applies to the underlying module of $\mathcal A$. Reindex the resulting small filtered diagram by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-category-directed-cofinal] to obtain a small nonempty directed set $I$, finitely presented quasi-coherent modules $\mathcal F_i$, transitions $f_{ji}$, and a module colimit cocone $\varphi_i:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal A$. Absolute quasi-separatedness is exactly the hypothesis of the module approximation node.

By [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus], put $\mathcal S_i=\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F_i)$ and let $\psi_i:\mathcal S_i\to\mathcal A$ extend $\varphi_i$. The same universal property extends $j_jf_{ji}$ to $\sigma_{ji}:\mathcal S_i\to\mathcal S_j$. Checking on degree-one maps gives $\sigma_{ii}=1$, $\sigma_{hj}\sigma_{ji}=\sigma_{hi}$ and $\psi_j\sigma_{ji}=\psi_i$. Let $\mathcal J_i=\ker\psi_i$ and $\mathcal B_i=\operatorname{Im}\psi_i\subseteq\mathcal A$. The cited chart calculus gives quasi-coherence, $\mathcal B_i=\mathcal S_i/\mathcal J_i$, and the corresponding kernel, image and quotient on every affine etale chart. Compatibility gives $\sigma_{ji}(\mathcal J_i)\subseteq\mathcal J_j$ and $\mathcal B_i\subseteq\mathcal B_j$.

The inclusions $\mathcal B_i\to\mathcal A$ exhibit an algebra colimit. For an affine etale chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$, [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus] evaluates the module colimit of step 1 as $\mathcal A(U)=\varinjlim_i\mathcal F_i(U)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise], every $a\in\mathcal A(U)$ is $\varphi_{i,U}(x)$ for some $i,x$; hence it lies in $\mathcal B_i(U)$. Thus these subalgebras have union $\mathcal A(U)$. A compatible family of algebra maps on them extends uniquely to the union by assigning to $a\in\mathcal B_i(U)$ its given image; a common upper bound proves independence of $i$ and preservation of addition and multiplication. The chart colimit criterion of the first cited node now gives $\mathcal A=\varinjlim_i\mathcal B_i$ in quasi-coherent algebra sheaves.

For every $i$, apply [lem-sfb-space-module-fp-directed-approximation] to $\mathcal J_i$, and [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-category-directed-cofinal] to its index category: choose $\mathcal J_i=\varinjlim_{k\in K_i}\mathcal E_{ik}$ with $K_i$ small nonempty directed and each $\mathcal E_{ik}$ finitely presented. Denote the cocone maps by $e_{ik}:\mathcal E_{ik}\to\mathcal J_i$. Let $\mathcal L_{ik}$ be the ideal of $\mathcal S_i$ generated by the composite $\mathcal E_{ik}\to\mathcal J_i\hookrightarrow\mathcal S_i$, and set $\mathcal Q_{ik}=\mathcal S_i/\mathcal L_{ik}$. By [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus] these ideals and quotients are quasi-coherent, computed on affine etale charts by the generated ideals and ordinary quotients, and have the algebra quotient universal property. Since $\mathcal L_{ik}\subseteq\mathcal J_i$, there is a canonical map $b_{ik}:\mathcal Q_{ik}\to\mathcal B_i$.

Every $\mathcal Q_{ik}$ is finitely presented as an algebra. On an affine etale $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$, [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus] makes $M=\mathcal F_i(U)$ and $N=\mathcal E_{ik}(U)$ finitely presented $R$-modules, and identifies $\mathcal Q_{ik}(U)$ with $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ modulo the ideal generated by the image of $N$. A finite generating list for $N$ maps to a finite ideal-generating list. Clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-finite-presentation] therefore gives a finite polynomial presentation of $\mathcal Q_{ik}(U)$ over $R$. This is the algebra finite-presentation condition of the item; no finite presentation of its underlying module is asserted.

On the small nonempty set $P=\{(i,k):i\in I,\ k\in K_i\}$ define $(i,k)\preceq(j,l)$ when $i\le j$ and $\sigma_{ji}(\mathcal L_{ik})\subseteq\mathcal L_{jl}$. Identity and composition of $\sigma$ give reflexivity and transitivity. If $k\le l$ in $K_i$, compatibility of $e_{ik}$ gives $\mathcal L_{ik}\subseteq\mathcal L_{il}$, so every row is monotone. For $i\le j$ the map $\mathcal E_{ik}\to\mathcal J_i\to\mathcal J_j$ factors through some $\mathcal E_{jl}$ by [lem-sfb-space-fp-module-hom-colimit]. Its domain is finitely presented, and its target is the module-sheaf colimit chosen in step 4 on the same qcqs space. This factorization implies the required containment of generated ideals, hence $(i,k)\preceq(j,l)$. Given two pairs, choose a common upper $j$ of their first coordinates, move both to row $j$ by this factorization, and then take a common upper bound of their second coordinates in $K_j$. Thus $P$ is directed. For $p=(i,k)\preceq q=(j,l)$ the quotient universal property in [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus] uniquely gives $\alpha_{qp}:\mathcal Q_{ik}\to\mathcal Q_{jl}$ with $\alpha_{qp}q_{ik}=q_{jl}\sigma_{ji}$, where $q_{ik}$ denotes the quotient projection. The same uniqueness gives identity and composition laws, as well as $b_{jl}\alpha_{qp}=(\mathcal B_i\hookrightarrow\mathcal B_j)b_{ik}$.

For fixed $i$, the cocone $b_{ik}:\mathcal Q_{ik}\to\mathcal B_i$ is colimiting. On each affine etale $U$, chart evaluation of step 4 and [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] imply that every element of $\mathcal J_i(U)$ comes from some $\mathcal E_{ik}(U)$. Consequently $\bigcup_k\mathcal L_{ik}(U)=\mathcal J_i(U)$: one containment follows from the definition of the kernel ideal, and the other from these representatives. The ideals in this union are increasing along $K_i$. For any compatible family of algebra maps from $\mathcal S_i(U)/\mathcal L_{ik}(U)$, their composites with $\mathcal S_i(U)$ agree, by a common upper bound in $K_i$ and the quotient formulas in step 6. Their common composite kills the union $\mathcal J_i(U)$, so factors uniquely through $\mathcal S_i(U)/\mathcal J_i(U)=\mathcal B_i(U)$. Conversely a map from that quotient gives such a family. The chart colimit criterion of [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus] gives the asserted row colimit in algebra sheaves.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-directed-pairs-colimit-transitivity] in the category of quasi-coherent commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras, with $D(i,k)=\mathcal Q_{ik}$ and $B(i)=\mathcal B_i$. Its conditions (a), (b), (c) are respectively the first-coordinate condition in the definition of $\preceq$, row monotonicity, and the factorization assertion of step 6. The compatibility equation is the last equation of that step, its row-colimit hypothesis is step 7, and its outer colimit is step 3. It follows that the maps $\mathcal Q_{ik}\to\mathcal B_i\hookrightarrow\mathcal A$ form a colimit cocone. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-category-directed-cofinal] applied to the small filtered preorder $P$ reindexes this cocone by a small nonempty directed set if an antisymmetric index order is required. All its terms retain the finite algebra presentations of step 5, and all arrows and cocone maps retain their laws. This is the cocone in the statement.
